summary: Blob storage, streaming and atomic positions are well specified; the biggest gap is exactly which changes make a stored sync position incompatible, followed by how surfaces attach file paths and resolve a BlobRef's originating instance.

questions.text: What exact text format does FetchContext.startedAt use (ISO 8601 with Z, precision), or should it be a typed instant?
questions.reason: Plugins parse it for backfill and retention windows; 0029 calls it 'one host-captured UTC instant' but types it Text, while 0007 says instants are 'Documented strings, checked by corresponding SDK type'.

questions.text: How is the local file path attached to each BlobRef in CLI/MCP results (sibling field, side table or wrapper), and do generated MCP output schemas include it?
questions.reason: The path is not part of the checked contract that MCP schemas are generated from; 0029 'supplies a read-only local file path alongside each reference' and 0018 'usable blob exports' give no shape.

questions.text: Does 'read-only local file path' mean Kyyn sets blob files read-only, or only that callers must not modify them?
questions.reason: An edited blob silently stops matching its sha256, but enforcing modes changes storage writes and cleanup; 0029 says only 'read-only', and 0016 notes Kyyn does not manage permissions for secrets.

questions.text: Which changes make a stored sync position incompatible: its contract, any plugin source change, package identity, or an instance configuration edit?
questions.reason: Too broad a rule forces full resyncs on every fix, too narrow reuses cursors under changed behaviour; 0029 'Changed code/contract must never reuse an incompatible position', 0014 'bound to producing plugin source and payload contract' and, for Files only, 'A changed source configuration starts a new producer'.

questions.text: ADR 0029 adds an acquisition-only digestText request, but ADR 0009's AcquisitionRequests sum has no digest constructor and its ReadsEvidence instance injects at a fixed depth.
questions.reason: Generated adapters, injection depths and broker dispatch depend on the exact row; 0029 'digestText :: [Text] -> Acquisition payload [Text]' vs 0009 'AcquisitionRequests payload = Http :+: (BlobAcquisition :+: (Secrets :+: (Waiting :+: (FileRead :+: EvidenceRead payload))))'.

questions.text: How does the host determine each BlobRef's originating captured instance in a composed KB-tool result, given that BlobRef has no instance field?
questions.reason: This is the boundary that refuses references outside the captured instance, and the same hash may exist in two instances; 0029 'Resolution uses the originating captured instance ... A forged or unresolvable reference is a diagnostic'.

questions.text: May BlobRef appear in accepted root facts, query results or recipe state, and if so how are those references resolved or validated?
questions.reason: A fact citing a blob would point into a disposable per-instance cache; 0005 makes BlobReference a general Shape, while 0029 says the path is 'not a citation, a KB fact' and that 'recipe state do[es] not retain bytes'.

questions.text: Does reclamation sweep every unreferenced file in blobs/ and payloads/, or delete only the files the current publication released?
questions.reason: Garbage left by interrupted cleanup is only collected if some step scans the directory; 0014 step 4 'Reclaim payloads and blobs no longer referenced by the published index' and 0029 'Interrupted cleanup may leave garbage for a subsequent cleanup'.
